newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares fall ahead of U.S. Thanksgiving.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares fall ahead of U.S. Thanksgiving.

text.p: Leading Russian shares fell on Wednesday in quiet trade before the U.S. Thanksgiving holidays, traders said.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares slipped by 1.76 percent to 187.14 on $8.83 million in volume.
"There is no interest in buying even at low prices," said Alexei Goncharov, an analyst at Russian Brokerage House.
He said that while leading shares, preferred shares and second-tier stocks were slipping, there was interest in second-tier preferred shares due to their high dividends.

Goncharov forecast the market drifting down slowly with an average daily fall of three percent, unless a meeting between Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and International Monetary Fund manager Michel Camdessus on Wednesday in Paris was successful.
"If they reach an agreement, prices will rise tomorrow on local speculation; if not prices will fall because of the Thanksgiving holidays," he said.
U.S. markets are closed on Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday.
He said the only news that could move the market up before the end of the year was if the IMF decided to pay Russia the next tranche of its $10 billion loan.
Victor Pitaleff, a Renaissance Capital trader, said news about a possible Moscow City Telephone (MGTS) Eurobond issue in the second quarter of 1997 had had no impact on the market.
He said it would take investors several weeks to digest the news before deciding to buy.
Gazprom fell to $0.367 from $0.368 at Tuesday's close, Norilsk Nickel was 5.90 after $5.85 and Rostelekom slipped to $2.31 from $2.32.
UES was $0.0817 after $0.0822 and MGTS -- long Russia's highest-priced share -- was $750.00 after $800.000 at Friday's close when it was last traded.
